newsitem.title: MONGOLIA: Mongolia begins liberalisation of energy prices.
newsitem.headline: Mongolia begins liberalisation of energy prices.

text.p: Mongolia raised prices of oil on Sunday in the first step of a programme to free energy prices and jumpstart the wheezing power industry before the arrival of harsh steppeland winter.
Legislators were drafting major reforms to gradually free state-fixed energy prices from September 1 and boost efficiency in the power sector, Prime Minister M. Enkhsaikhan said.
"The government needs to liberalise energy prices," Enkhsaikhan said in a speech to parliament on Friday.
Revenue increases from higher prices would ease work to boost fuel reserves to a safe level for the winter and would finance badly-needed repairs of power plants, he said.
Petrol stations in the capital Ulan Bator raised fuel prices by up to one-third, apparently in line with the graudual liberalistion.
The price of 96 octane petrol rose to 170 tugriks (about US 32 cts) per litre from 126 tugriks and diesel to 200 tugriks from 150 tugriks.

The state had been losing money on imports of petroleum products since October 1995 and imports had fallen sharply, Enkhsaikhan said, adding the market was being supported by rapidly dwindling state reserves.
Mongolia imports 100 percent of its petroleum.
The government had poured 28.8 billion tugriks in subsidies into the power and heating industries in 1995, an amount equal to eight percent of Mongolia's GDP, he said.
"This situation shows that instead of renewing equipment and upgrading technology we are wasting foreign funds on covering losses," he said.
